Re-fit with the procedure in simulator/README.md if the baseline parameters change. Cases outside the reach are handled exactly as in the baseline arm (same random numbers), so they carry no owner, no timers, no escalation and can be lost silently.
overrides.source: Calibrated so the orchestrated/baseline completion ratio at 180 days equals navigation_effect = 1.27 (pooled RR 1.27, 95% CI 1.10-1.46, 8 navigation studies, moderate certainty, J Gen Intern Med 2026, PMID 42618855, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11606-026-10706-x; 12-month RCT: 55.1% vs 42.1%, Annals 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13007779/). Fit of 2026-10-18 (refit after A18 milestones and A19 coalescing): 0.55 gives a literature-anchored 180-day completion ratio of 1.272 (66.3% against 52.1%; 0.54 gives 1.268, 0.56 gives 1.276). Procedure and fitted ratios: docs/results/results.md.
Capped at patient_response.dropout_residual_multiplier (0.25): a human call does not re-engage a disengaged patient better than a digital re-contact.

overrides.notes: Upper-range value 0.25 (Lam et al. 2021, relative reduction 11.9% -> 8.9%). At 0 the orchestrated arm's no-show is the no-reminder rate dna_rate (0.119) for every patient, which is above the baseline's 0.089 for SMS and phone patients (those baseline rates already embed Lam's SMS arm); the scenario therefore slightly understates orchestrated attendance for them. Left as is: we do not re-estimate the baseline.
overrides.source: Lower bound of the sensitivity range in docs/evidence.md section 4: Mahmud et al., JAMA Netw Open 2021 (753 patients, nine text messages, no effect on attendance with good prep, 53.1% vs 54.4%, P=.73). https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.34553
